CANADIAN RINK CONTROLLER DIRECTORY · CHECKED OCTOBER 24, 2026

Know what’s covered.

Twelve playable controller profiles, with installation evidence, manuals and transparent model gaps. Start with the brand and overlay on your rink’s console; a scoreboard brand alone does not identify the controls.

No national installed-controller registry has been found. This is a documented roster, not a claim that every Canadian rink or firmware variant is covered. Local guides may be dated; confirm the equipment at your arena.

Daktronics All Sport 5000PlayableMitchell, Ontario; Carleton University, OttawaInstallation / market evidence ↗Manual / reference ↗Hockey overlay LL-2436; installed firmware can differ.
Hamilton VisionTimePlayablePanorama Recreation Centre, British ColumbiaInstallation / market evidence ↗Manual / reference ↗VisionTime telephone keypad and function-key layout.
Hamilton HDD 2000PlayableCambridge, Ontario (2016 guide)Installation / market evidence ↗Manual / reference ↗Separate calculator-keypad workflow; not VisionTime.
OES ISC9000PlayablePort Elgin, OntarioInstallation / market evidence ↗Manual / reference ↗Four penalty rows; two active; training configuration documented.
OES ISC85XPlayableBell Sensplex and Richcraft Sensplex, OntarioInstallation / market evidence ↗Manual / reference ↗Preset minutes and rocker switch; optional play timer omitted.
Nevco MPC · hockey code 871PlayableKemptville, OntarioInstallation / market evidence ↗Manual / reference ↗871 is a configuration, not a hardware generation. Check the physical overlay before selecting.
Nevco MPC-4 · K2-28PlayableKitsilano, British ColumbiaInstallation / market evidence ↗Manual / reference ↗Hockey overlay K2-28, configuration 008-3261. No shot clocks. Alternate switch works only with no handheld attached. Ten penalties per side are a trainer limit; hardware has larger per-player memory. Clock modes here expose local time only; automatic startup programs and auxiliary clocks are omitted. Exact-score entry follows the local single-digit guide, with TIME returning to the clock.
Nevco MPCW-7PlayableRussell, OntarioInstallation / market evidence ↗Manual / reference ↗2016 hockey overlay, wired panel time control with no handheld attached. Default minor 2:00, major 5:00; penalty on/off enabled. Main MMSSs commits after five digits; period is separate. Timeout timer 1 is fixed to 30 seconds, displayed on the practice scoreboard; warning options and other timeout timers are omitted. Radio pairing, profiles, installation options, team-name programming and shot clocks are outside this profile. Goal light duration is a practice default.
Fair-Play MP-50 / MP-70Playable · layout pendingRay Friel, Ottawa, Ontario (family identified; model suffix unverified)Installation / market evidence ↗Manual / reference ↗MP-50/70 common hockey workflow; fixed 2/5/10-minute presets, five penalties per side, no 10-minute indicator spots, goal indicators enabled. The manufacturer photo shows the housing with a basketball overlay. Hockey key groups are a functional training arrangement; exact hockey overlay positions remain unverified. OTHER multi-segment penalties, program menus, timeout configuration, interval configuration, shifted penalty tracking and automatic penalty-time correction are omitted. Correcting the main clock preserves penalty times in this trainer.
Scoretec Ultimatic U1000PlayableCoquitlam, British Columbia; Calgary, AlbertaInstallation / market evidence ↗Manual / reference ↗U1000 control family with shots and player-number display, as described in the manufacturer manual. Five penalty slots per team, two active. Staging uses minutes or M:SS with optional /player. Long holds on CLEAR and STOP/GO PENALTIES take five seconds. Interval mode 1 and count-up limit mode 2 are implemented; full interval programming, time-of-day setup and team timeouts are omitted. Naden appears in the hosted manual title; that does not establish that every Naden console is a U1000.
Harris Time SportstimerPlayableCambridge, Ontario: Dickson, Duncan McIntosh, Hespeler and Preston (2016 guide)Installation / market evidence ↗Manual / reference ↗Photographed Cambridge Sportstimer variant; unlocked at the start of practice. TIME and INT accept up to 20:00; periods 0–4; penalties up to five slots per side. Practice scoreboard displays two active slots and queues the rest. Slot labels stand in for player numbers because this panel enters a slot, not a jersey. Manual horn uses HORN 0 #; 2/3-minute horn must be configured each period. Exact Type 1 versus Type 2 mapping is unverified. HI indicator programming, passkey and physical unlock behavior are omitted.
Rotomatic A3004-PTPlayableKarl Homuth Arena, Cambridge, Ontario (2016 guide)Installation / market evidence ↗Manual / reference ↗Legacy A3004-PT label visible in the local guide photograph. Separate tens/units score buttons and two physical penalty timers per team, without jersey entry or an automatic queue. MAIN TIME switch plus START arms the clock. AUTO HORN is the interval toggle, separate from the automatic five-second end horn. Main RESET also sounds the horn. Mechanical key auto-repeat, electromechanical latency and contact behavior are not emulated. No manufacturer manual located; operation is sourced to the local rink guide and photographed panel instructions.
Harris Time Type 1 / Type 2Research gapCanadian manufacturer; Cambridge Harris installations documented, exact type mapping unresolvedInstallation / market evidence ↗Manual / reference ↗Separate manufacturer instructions exist. The playable Sportstimer represents the photographed Cambridge variant only.
OES ISC EdgeResearch gapCanadian manufacturer, hockey manual available; exact Canadian rink installation not yet verifiedInstallation / market evidence ↗Manual / reference ↗Touchscreen/controller generation differs from ISC9000. Needs its own simulator and installation evidence.
OES ISC-HHXResearch gapCanadian manufacturer; exact rink installation not yet verifiedInstallation / market evidence ↗Manual / reference ↗Handheld interface; do not substitute an ISC85X or ISC9000 keypad.
Fair-Play MP-60 / MP-80Research gapHockey-capable product; exact Canadian rink installation not yet verifiedInstallation / market evidence ↗Manual / reference ↗Separate generation from MP-50/70. Product page links the manual and product imagery.
Daktronics All Sport 3000Research gapHockey-capable legacy controller; exact Canadian rink installation not yet verifiedInstallation / market evidence ↗Manual / reference ↗Different sport insert and startup codes; not the All Sport 5000 profile.
Daktronics All Sport 2000 / 2600Research gapHockey-capable legacy family; exact Canadian rink installation not yet verifiedInstallation / market evidence ↗Manual / reference ↗Legacy sport-code and panel variants need verification before simulation.

Other leads: Spectrum, Sportable / Varsity, Colorado Time SystemsResearch gapCanadian rink use and hockey configuration unverifiedInstallation / market evidence ↗Manual / reference ↗Community inventory is a research lead only; it is not Canadian installation evidence or a verified manual.

To document an additional controller, collect the console model label, full hockey overlay photo, arena and province, and the matching operating manual. Do not infer an installed controller from a scoreboard model or a reseller listing.
